title: Planning documents and communications for the launch of America.gov

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Planning documents and communications for the launch of America.gov
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

I would like to request emails, planning documents, timelines and other communications related to the launch of America.gov in late September 2026. These communications would likely be in the 3 months prior to October 1st, 2026 and involve staff from General Services Administration as well as the National Design Studio. These communications would likely involve the following staff (but not exclusively) from GSA and the National Design Studio: Sam Corcos, Edward Coristine, Joe Gebbia, Sully Vickers. It should also include staff detailed to GSA from IRS, including Ryan Parker and Justin Adelman. It could also include National Design Studio staff Jaylee Adams, Abdulwahab Omira, James DeBrock, Edward Christine, Kaitlen Koller, Aaron Jackson, Michael Novia, Darshan Phillips, Braden Steffaniak and Aldous Waites.

I would also like to request any resignation letters or communications from staff that they are leaving work on America.gov. These would likely include the staff named above or others who might mention America.gov specifically.

I would like to request any communications or discussions about the code quality of America.gov. These might be emails or issues on Github or wherever the source code for the project is hosted internally. This request should also include code chat transcripts with AI services like Claude Code, Grok, or Gemini from America.gov developers Edward Corisitine, Sam Corcos, Ryan Parker, Jared Zoneraich and Justin Adelman

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jacob Harris

title: HackerRank testing for IRS Technical Staff

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: HackerRank testing for IRS Technical Staff
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

In an article published on 12/2/2025, Wired Magazine reported that Sam Corcos had ordered that all agency staff must take tests on the HackerRank code screening site. More recently, in the book "Blockers," the author Michael Lewis quoted Sam Corcos complaining that most agency technical staff had flunked these assessments.

1. I would like to request more information about which assessments were used with agency staff and the evaluation results (individual scores would be useful but I understand those might need to be redacted). I am also good to receive aggregate results to indicate how internal divisions scored on these assessments.
2. I would like to request any communications on how these assessments were selected for staff, and if they were tailored for specific employee skillsets or just set globally. These communications would likely be to/from CIO Sam Corcos.
3. I would like to request any information on how this HackerRank service was procured. These were also likely directed and organized by CIO Sam Corcos.
4. Finally, I would like to request any internal communications on how low scores on HackerRank were used as justification for terminating employment. These also would have involved Sam Corcos as well as Human Resources staff at the IRS. There might also be communications to staff at OPM.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jacob Harris
